observationsForTheReviewer: The proof is runnable in a Legion pod after all. The implementer recorded, and the plan's D7 assumed, that no worker machine has a container runtime and so the live proof can run only in CI. True of testcontainers, not of the proof: `GOWORK=off GOBIN=/tmp/bin go install github.com/nats-io/nats-server/v2@v2.15.1` builds the hub's own pinned server version as a plain binary in this pod, and the listener then runs against it on 127.0.0.1:4222. Nothing in this change needs fixing for that; it is worth knowing for the next Envoy issue whose proof is assumed CI-only.

core.CheckAllowedHosts is one class stricter than the listener's own rule: an entry with surrounding whitespace, or an empty entry, is refused at preview where the listener would trim or skip it (165 of 23,630 corpus entries, all of that one class; zero in the opposite, hub-down direction). The strictness is protective — a space would split the unit's docker run argument — but the PR body's 'in exactly the cases the listener refuses one at boot', the same sentence in docs/nats-hub.md, and TestCoreAndTheListenerAgreeOnAnAllowedHost's own doc comment ('every entry either side refuses, the other refuses') each state a two-way property that holds only for un-padded entries. A whitespace row in that table would pin the asymmetry as deliberate.

A request whose target is in absolute form and names the hub (`POST http://example-hub.example-tailnet.ts.net:9020/v1/… HTTP/1.1` with `Host: evil.example.invalid`) is served 200, because Go's net/http takes r.Host from the request target. That is the listener guard's own pre-existing behaviour, not this change's, and no browser can send that form; recorded because this change is the first to give the hub a non-loopback name to be reached by.
